content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy with a creamy filling is a small sweet coated in milk or dark chocolate and filled with a smooth buttercream. It is made from cocoa mass, sugar, dairy ingredients and flavorings. The candies are usually packaged in portioned boxes and are a popular treat in offices, schools and celebrations.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recipe for cream‑filled chocolate candies appeared in early 20th‑century Europe.
The filling can be vanilla, caramel, nut‑based or fruit‑flavored depending on the brand.
Chocolate candies are often used as ingredients in desserts such as cakes and ice‑cream.
In some countries the candies are classified as “dairy products,” which affects taxation.
Dark‑chocolate versions contain more antioxidants than milk‑chocolate ones.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa mass in chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium present in cocoa supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, which can improve mood.

items.title: Calcium from dairy filling
items.content: The cream, made from milk, adds calcium important for bone health.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Sugar and fat in the candy provide rapid energy for the body.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: The filling often contains milk, making the candy unsuitable for people with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: Some manufacturers use partially hydrogenated oils that contain trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Chocolate contains small amounts of stimulants that can affect sleep in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candies are convenient as a standalone snack, can be added to dessert mixes, sprinkled over ice‑cream, or used in baking. For children, offer small portions to avoid excessive sugar intake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in a cool, dry place in an airtight container to prevent chocolate melt‑down and absorption of external odors. At temperatures above 25 °C chocolate may soften and the cream can separate.

content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated instant coffee is a dry powder made from roasted and extracted coffee beans from which caffeine has been removed. The powder requires no water addition and is ready to consume as a finished beverage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Instant coffee was introduced in the early 20th century and quickly gained popularity for its convenience.
Caffeine is removed using Swiss‑water or CO₂ extraction methods, which preserve most flavor compounds.
Decaffeinated instant coffee often contains stabilizers and flavor enhancers to improve taste.
The low moisture content allows the powder to be stored longer than ground coffee.
In many countries, decaf instant coffee is classified as a "coffee extract beverage".

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: The absence of caffeine makes the drink suitable for caffeine‑sensitive individuals and for evening consumption.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Despite caffeine removal, the powder retains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Compounds such as chlorogenic acid may help regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Portion control and convenience
items.content: Single‑serve packets allow precise measurement, aiding calorie control.

items.title: Reduced cardiovascular risk
items.content: Regular moderate coffee consumption, including decaf, is linked to a lower risk of hypertension.

items.title: Additives and flavorings
items.content: Some brands use artificial flavors and sweeteners that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Acrylamide content
items.content: Roasting creates small amounts of acrylamide, a potential carcinogen, though levels in instant coffee are generally low.

items.title: Possible stomach discomfort
items.content: Even without caffeine, coffee can irritate the stomach lining in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added sugar or salt in ready mixes
items.content: Pre‑flavored mixes may contain added sugar or salt, increasing caloric load.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dissolve 1‑2 g of powder in 200 ml of hot water (80‑90 °C). Add milk, plant‑based drinks, sweetener, or spices (cinnamon, cardamom) to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the packet in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, seal tightly to prevent moisture absorption and flavor loss.

content.title: About
content.content: Hot chocolate (cocoa) is a beverage made from cocoa powder, sugar, and milk or water. It offers a rich chocolate flavor, aroma, and a warming effect. It is often served with whipped cream, marshmallows, or spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cocoa beans were first domesticated in Mesoamerica over 3,000 years ago.
The term “hot chocolate” appeared in Europe in the 16th century after cocoa was brought from the New World.
Cocoa contains more than 600 biologically active compounds, including theobromine and flavonoids.
In some countries hot chocolate is traditionally made with dark chocolate rather than cocoa powder.
There are many variations: with cinnamon, vanilla, mint, chili, and even sea salt.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa flavonoids help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Theobromine and phenylethylamine promote endorphin release, improving mood.

items.title: Blood pressure reduction
items.content: Moderate regular cocoa consumption may lead to a modest drop in blood pressure.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Cocoa provides magnesium, iron, zinc, and potassium, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Cognitive support
items.content: Studies suggest flavonoids can help maintain memory and attention.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Hot chocolate is often prepared with a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and elevated blood glucose.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: These stimulants may cause insomnia or rapid heartbeat in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Dairy‑based versions may be unsuitable for people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Cocoa powder can irritate the stomach of those with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix cocoa powder into hot water or milk, add sugar or a sweetener to taste. Top with whipped cream, marshmallows, a sprinkle of cinnamon or grated chocolate. For a vegan version, use plant‑based milk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cocoa powder in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored, it retains flavor for up to 2 years. Milk‑based mixes should be refrigerated and used within a few days.

content.title: About
content.content: Light chocolate ice cream is a low‑fat dessert made from skimmed milk, reduced‑fat cream, sugar and natural cocoa. It retains a rich chocolate flavor while delivering fewer calories than traditional ice cream.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Often used in diet plans because of its reduced calorie count.
Chocolate flavor is achieved with cocoa mass and natural flavorings without added vegetable fats.
Stabilizers such as gelatin or pectin are sometimes added to keep a creamy texture with low fat.
The product can be fortified with B‑vitamins and calcium to boost its nutritional profile.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Reduced fat content helps lower the overall calorie load, supporting weight management.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Dairy ingredients provide calcium essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa is rich in flavonoids, which may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugar and carbohydrates quickly replenish glycogen stores, offering a rapid energy lift.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should choose alternative options.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite low fat, the sugar level can be high, which is important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even with fewer calories than regular ice cream, overconsumption can still lead to excess energy intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve light chocolate ice cream in individual cups or as scoops. It pairs well with berries, nuts, or a drizzle of honey for added flavor variety.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the ice cream at –18 °C in an airtight container. After opening, consume within 2–3 days to maintain texture and flavor.

nutritional-drink-or-shake-ready-to-drin.title: Nutritional drink or shake, ready-to-drink (Muscle Milk)

content.title: About
content.content: Muscle Milk is a ready‑to‑drink protein shake designed to support muscle growth and post‑workout recovery. It typically contains milk proteins (whey and casein), carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals. The product is available in a variety of flavors and packaging sizes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Muscle Milk protein shake was launched in the United States in 2005.
The brand markets the product as a "nutritional drink" rather than just a sports supplement.
Formulations often include performance‑enhancing additives such as creatine and BCAA.
Muscle Milk is sold in more than 20 countries worldwide.
Some variants are fortified with probiotics to support gut health.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: A single serving usually provides 20‑25 g of protein, which helps muscle building and repair.

items.title: Complete amino acid profile
items.content: Whey and casein proteins deliver both fast‑acting and sustained amino acid release.

items.title: Energy replenishment
items.content: Carbohydrates such as maltodextrin or fructose quickly restore glycogen stores.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The drink contains calcium, vitamin D, vitamin B12 and magnesium, supporting bone and nerve function.

items.title: Convenient consumption
items.content: The ready‑to‑drink format provides a quick source of nutrients without preparation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Contains whey and casein, which may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Some flavors contain up to 15 g of sugar per serving, which may be undesirable for those monitoring sugar intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A single bottle can provide 200‑300 kcal; frequent consumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Certain versions use sucralose or aspartame, which some consumers prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the shake immediately after mixing, ideally within 30‑60 minutes post‑workout. It can also serve as a quick snack between meals, diluted with water or milk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the ready‑to‑drink bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, refrigerate and consume within 24 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato tots are small bite‑size pieces of grated potato that are coated in a seasoned breadcrumb crust, flash‑frozen and ready for quick cooking. They become golden and crispy when baked or deep‑fried while staying soft inside.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato tots were introduced in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a convenient snack.
They are a staple in fast‑food restaurants, school cafeterias, and as a bar side dish.
Freezing locks in flavor and texture, allowing them to be cooked directly from the freezer.
Many flavor variations exist, including cheese‑filled, bacon‑infused, and herb‑spiced versions.
Tots are often featured in cooking contests for their simplicity and versatility.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: A modest amount of vitamin C survives the processing, providing antioxidant benefits.

items.title: Quick‑release carbohydrates
items.content: Tots supply fast‑acting carbs that can fuel physical activity.

items.title: Low sodium (when unsalted)
items.content: If the product is sold without added salt, it can fit a low‑sodium diet.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Grated potato retains some fiber, which aids digestion.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because of the breading and oil, tots are relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Possible trans‑fat content
items.content: Some brands may use partially hydrogenated oils; choose trans‑fat‑free options when possible.

items.title: Potato allergy (rare)
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to potatoes or to additives in the coating.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Prepared tots often contain added salt; individuals with hypertension should opt for low‑salt varieties.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) or heat oil to 180 °C (350 °F). Spread the frozen tots in a single layer on a baking sheet, lightly spray with oil and bake 12‑15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp. In a deep fryer, cook 3‑4 minutes until browned. Serve hot with ketchup, aioli, or your favorite dipping sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen tots in their original packaging in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F). After opening, reseal the bag tightly to prevent freezer burn. Cooked tots should be stored in the refrigerator and eaten within 2‑3 days.
